items.title: Strikes, Barricades and Fiscal Turmoil: An Autumn of Discontent Grips France
items.summary: Chaos in schools, on the streets and in the markets is rooted in France’s struggles to fund its social welfare state, with a presidential election approaching.

items.title: India Cut 130 Million From Voter Roll, Fueling Protests Against Modi
items.summary: Public anger is growing over an exercise that critics say undermines the world’s largest democracy, particularly disenfranchising Muslims under the Hindu nationalist government.

items.title: As Japan’s Population Shrinks, a City Is Accused of Padding Census Numbers
items.summary: The police are investigating how about 3,000 nonexistent residents were added to official data for Toyama.

items.title: Lawmakers Set to Elect Germany’s 1st Far-Right Statehouse Speaker Since 1945
items.summary: After winning a state election last month, the AfD is now on the cusp of being the first far-right party to oversee a state Parliament since the Nazi era.

items.title: FIFA Found Congo Player Ineligible, Let Him Play in World Cup
items.summary: Officials determined that a goalkeeper from the Democratic Republic of Congo did not have the correct paperwork, documents show. But no action was taken, renewing questions about FIFA’s governance.

items.title: South Korea Investigates Possible Use of A.I. in Hacks on Its Banks
items.summary: The president said there were signs that such models were used in recent attacks on several banks involving customer data. Police are investigating.

items.title: France Set for Nationwide Strikes, as School Protests Escalate
items.summary: The scale of the demonstrations planned for Tuesday will test the strength of the student-led protest movement that has spread across French high schools since late September.

items.title: Russia Moves to Tamp Down Rumors About Plague Outbreak in Siberia
items.summary: The country’s consumer watchdog has said only that “an employee of an anti-plague institute in the Irkutsk Region” contracted pneumonia.

items.title: Brazil Election Could Give Bolsonaro a Key Role in Trump’s Latin America Map
items.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, now the favorite to win Brazil’s presidency, would give President Trump a critical new ally in Latin America, particularly on security.

items.title: Why Saudi Arabia’s Last War in Yemen Turned Into a Quagmire
items.summary: A Saudi-led coalition has announced a military campaign against the Iran-backed Houthi militia in the country, reviving memories of its previous effort.

items.title: The Hidden Policies That Power China’s Export Boom
items.summary: Huge tax breaks and a weak currency sustain exports, widen the government budget deficit and complicate the country’s efforts to rebalance its economy.

items.title: A.I. Officials Stonewall on Questions About Technology’s Risks
items.summary: A New York City Council hearing on artificial intelligence yielded few answers or assurances about how the industry would provide safeguards against catastrophic scenarios.

items.title: Trump Allows Cheaper, Dyed Diesel to Be Used in Nonfarm Vehicles
items.summary: In Nebraska, President Trump signed an executive order to waive an off-road requirement for the fuel, which is exempt from the federal highway tax.

items.title: Nashville Symphony Receives $10 Million Lifeline From Oracle
items.summary: The symphony announced last week that it was pausing the rest of the season after disclosing financial trouble. The concerts are back on now, thanks to a tech company gift.

items.title: High Interest Rates Aren’t Slowing the A.I. Boom. That’s a Problem for the Fed.
items.summary: Rising borrowing costs are taking a toll on households and businesses. But they are doing little to dampen enthusiasm for investments in A.I. infrastructure, which are contributing to inflation.

items.title: Texas Pediatricians Face Paxton Investigations for Vaccinating Children
items.summary: Ken Paxton, the Texas attorney general and Republican Senate candidate, has alleged a sprawling profit-driven conspiracy. Pediatricians say the accusations are an attempt at intimidation.

items.title: War With Iran Is Forcing the World to Reckon With Geography’s Power
items.summary: Trade blockages in the Persian Gulf have reminded the world that there are forces as great as or greater than technology and globalization.

items.title: Burst of Attacks in Gulf Heightens Fears Over Fragile Energy Trade
items.summary: Strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia came as the region’s exporters were getting more oil to the world market.

items.title: Karoline Leavitt, Trump’s ‘Machine Gun,’ Has a New Gig at Fox News
items.summary: A fierce and nimble speaker, Ms. Leavitt is the third of Mr. Trump’s former press secretaries to join the cable news network.

items.title: Inside Binance Founder Changpeng Zhao’s Life After Prison
items.summary: Changpeng Zhao, jailed in the United States for a financial crime and pardoned by President Trump, is now living a gilded life in the United Arab Emirates.

items.title: Who’s to Blame When A.I. Goes Rogue?
items.summary: Many think artificial intelligence companies should be held liable for their runaway technology. But legal scholars say applying existing law could be messy.

items.title: OpenAI’s Greg Brockman Backs Out of Second $25 Million Donation to A.I. Super PAC
items.summary: Greg Brockman, OpenAI’s president and co-founder, said internally that the super PAC, Leading the Future, had become a “distraction” for the A.I. company.

items.title: How Meta Uses A.I. Data Centers to Avoid Billions in Federal Taxes
items.summary: Meta is exploiting a lucrative tax break intended to support research and experimentation. Its own accountants say the gambit is risky.

items.title: The Humanoid Robot Future Has Arrived at a South Korean Park. Sort of.
items.summary: I went to Galaxy Robot Park in Seoul to see how we might one day live with robots. It was part cutting-edge technology, part theatrics.

items.title: US Solar Panel Makers Try to Catch China With a Big Leap in Technology
items.summary: Manufacturers say they are close to perfecting a new, more efficient solar panel that could help the United States reclaim ground it lost.

items.title: Are Babies Conscious?
items.summary: By pinpointing when it begins in young humans, scientists hope to better understand what consciousness is, and how it arises, in all of us.

items.title: Court Tosses ​​Sentence After A.I. Video of Victim ‘Forgiving’ His Killer Is Played
items.summary: An appellate court in Arizona threw out the prison sentence of a man convicted of manslaughter after an A.I.-generated video of his victim was played at a trial.

items.title: An A.I. Songwriting Experiment: Humans Against the Machine
items.summary: Five humans convened for a weekend to create new music from scratch. Could they do better than A.I.? Could you even tell the difference?
